reason: This passage (Exodus 1:15-22) describes Pharaoh commanding the Hebrew midwives to kill Hebrew male newborns, not Yahweh killing Hebrews. The text actually portrays a positive relationship with God: the midwives fear God (vayira'u et ha'Elohim) and refuse to obey Pharaoh's evil command because of this fear. God rewards their faithfulness by dealing well with them (vayeitav Elohim laMyalledot) and causing the Hebrew population to multiply. The text contains no claim about Yahweh killing Hebrews, no mention of improper worship as a cause of death, and no punishment from God for religious infidelity.
